channel.title: Use & Like: app news
channel.description: What changed in the apps you use, in our own words, with what it means for you and what to do about it.

item.title: 8 new lifestyle apps climbing the App Store this week
item.description: These lifestyle apps came out in the last 60 days and rose into the US App Store's Lifestyle charts this week, from BabyBackup: Baby Monitor to One Cent Start.

item.title: Uber Parking: how to book a parking spot in the Uber app
item.description: Uber now lets you find, book and pay for a spot in a garage or lot from a new Parking button in its app. It starts in 15 US cities and is coming to more than 400 cities in the US and Canada.

item.title: 8 new weather apps climbing the App Store this week
item.description: These weather apps came out in the last 60 days and rose into the US App Store's Weather charts this week, from Local Skies: Retro Weather to HIRKA: What to Wear Today.

item.title: Claude Fable 5.2 is out: faster and cheaper, with fewer needless blocks
item.description: Anthropic released Claude Fable 5.2, which it says writes up to 30% faster than Fable 5.1 and is better at coding, reasoning and reading images. It's available today; the sister model Mythos 5.2 is only for vetted organizations.

item.title: 7 new photo and video apps climbing the App Store this week
item.description: These photo and video apps came out in the last 60 days and rose into the US App Store's Photo & Video charts this week, from Flipcorder: Retro Camcorder to SharpStop Depth of Field Calc.

item.title: Venmo can now scan a receipt and split the bill by item
item.description: Venmo's new receipt scanning reads a photo of a bill, lists each item and lets you assign it to whoever ordered it. It adds everyone's share of tax and tip and sends the payment requests.

item.title: 7 new productivity apps climbing the App Store this week
item.description: These productivity apps came out in the last 60 days and rose into the US App Store's Productivity charts this week, from 2Do: To Do List & Task Manager to Foreweek: Weekly Planner.

item.title: Airalo eSIM: one install for every trip, no new eSIM each time
item.description: Airalo is rolling out a single eSIM that stays on your phone for all your trips over the coming months. You'll buy the package you need for each trip instead of installing a new eSIM every time.

item.title: 7 new design apps climbing the App Store this week
item.description: These design apps came out in the last 60 days and rose into the US App Store's Graphics & Design charts this week, from AltoPaint: Oil & Gouache to FoldTales: Duo Wallpapers.

item.title: Paramount+ and HBO Max bundle coming in early 2027
item.description: Skydance, which now owns both, plans to offer Paramount+ and HBO Max together for one price from early 2027. It hasn't given prices yet.

item.title: 7 new music apps climbing the App Store this week
item.description: These music apps came out in the last 60 days and rose into the US App Store's Music charts this week, from NostalgicPod to Tapko Harmony.

item.title: Instagram's AI age check now finds teens worldwide, even with an adult birthday
item.description: Meta is using AI worldwide to spot Instagram users it thinks are 13 to 17, even if they entered an adult birthday, and puts them in Teen Account settings. Parents in the US will see a video about it in their feed this month.

item.title: Free phone upgrade scam: the caller asks you to send the new phone back
item.description: Scammers call claiming to be your mobile network and offer a free upgrade. A real phone arrives, then a second call says it was sent by mistake, and a courier takes it to the scammers while you keep paying the contract.

item.title: Galaxy AI Premium: Samsung may charge $4.99 a month for new AI features
item.description: Code in One UI 9.5 points to a Galaxy AI Premium plan for $4.99 a month or $47.99 a year, SammyGuru found. Today's Galaxy AI features would stay free.

item.title: iPhone Duo Display Zoom missing after setup: you can't change it later
item.description: On the iPhone Duo you choose Display Zoom (default, medium or large) only during setup; Settings has no option to change it afterwards, unlike other iPhones. MacRumors confirmed it on iOS 27.2.

item.title: IvyPod turns your iPhone into a classic click-wheel music player
item.description: IvyPod plays your Apple Music library through a wheel-based look of the music players of the past, with lighting and haptics. It was #33 among all paid apps on the UK App Store on 9 November.

item.title: Grandeur Link puts your Mac's screen, keyboard and trackpad on your iPhone
item.description: Grandeur Link shows your Mac's screen on your iPhone and lets you control it with a trackpad and keyboard over your home network. It was #52 among paid Utilities apps on the US App Store on 9 November.

item.title: PaliCAD is a 3D CAD app for iPhone and iPad, without a subscription
item.description: PaliCAD lets you sketch in 2D and build 3D models by touch or Apple Pencil, offline, for a one-time price. It was #20 among paid Productivity apps on the US App Store on 9 November.

item.title: FocusBook starts a focus timer when you open your iPhone Duo
item.description: FocusBook is a focus timer that starts when you open your iPhone Duo and pauses when you fold it shut. It was #35 among paid Productivity apps on the US App Store on 9 November.

item.title: Cheiron tracks a bodybuilder's food, training and supplements in one app
item.description: Cheiron brings food logging, a lifting notebook, supplements, weight and cardio into one app, with separate macro targets for training and rest days. It was #26 among paid Health & Fitness apps on the US App Store on 9 November.

item.title: Chocka tells you how high to block each wheel to level your RV
item.description: Lay your phone on the floor and Chocka says, for each wheel, how high it needs to go and on which step of your leveling blocks. It was #52 among paid Travel apps on the US App Store on 9 November.

item.title: CalenCards plans your day as a deck of cards instead of a calendar grid
item.description: CalenCards lays out your day as colorful cards you swipe away when done, aimed at people who find calendars cluttered. It was #97 among paid Productivity apps on the US App Store on 9 November.

item.title: DeskOS turns your iPhone into a small desktop with files, browser and editors
item.description: DeskOS gives your iPhone a desktop-style workspace with files, a browser and photo and video editors, with a keyboard and trackpad on screen. It was #91 among paid Productivity apps on the US App Store on 9 November.

item.title: GigClick is a metronome with setlists for bands, built by a drummer
item.description: GigClick keeps a click from 20 to 300 BPM, with setlists you can run on stage, and corrects the delay of Bluetooth headphones. It was #16 among paid Music apps on the US App Store on 9 November.

item.title: Eyes Down turns your iPhone into a bingo caller with a board on the TV
item.description: Eyes Down calls bingo numbers from your iPhone or iPad and shows the ball and board on a TV or projector, while your controls stay on your device. It was #81 among paid Entertainment apps on the US App Store on 9 November.

item.title: iSyn Tron brings back the 2009 iSyn groovebox for iPhone and iPad
item.description: iSyn Tron rebuilds iSyn, a groovebox app from 2009, with its original sound engine: two synths and an 8-track drum machine. It was #81 among paid Music apps on the US App Store on 9 November.

item.title: Outlook.com and Hotmail not receiving some emails since 5 November
item.description: Some Outlook.com and Hotmail users aren't getting emails because messages to them bounce, and senders are told they failed an SPF authentication check, even when their settings are correct. Windows Latest reproduced it on 8 November.

item.title: Free ChatGPT Pro invite scam: fake OpenAI event page steals your logins
item.description: A fake OpenAI Academy page invites you to a 4 November marketing livestream and promises three months of ChatGPT Pro, but it's built to steal Microsoft and Google logins, security firm Push Security found.

item.title: Cheap Netflix and Spotify subscriptions from resellers come with risks
item.description: A Surfshark study found reseller sites sell streaming subscriptions for an average of $4.60 a month instead of $13.13, but often with shared accounts, long upfront commitments and less control.

item.title: Black Friday scam: 10,000 fake shopping sites, some showing up in AI answers
item.description: NordVPN found a network of more than 10,000 fake shop websites copying 166 fashion and luxury brands in 26 countries, and some have appeared in search results and AI shopping recommendations next to real shops.

item.title: iPhone Duo scam: fake online stores offer the foldable iPhone at a discount
item.description: Kaspersky found fake websites selling the sold-out iPhone Duo, including one in Apple's style offering 25% off with a 30-minute countdown; buyers lose their money and card details.

item.title: Tots Weather tells you what to dress your child in today
item.description: Tots Weather turns the local forecast into a straight answer: what your child should wear right now for what you're about to do. It was #12 among paid Lifestyle apps on the US App Store on 7 November.

item.title: MediateMe helps you explain yourself in tricky conversations
item.description: MediateMe is a calm, turn-based app that gives a bottom-line analysis of a disagreement and suggests messages tailored to how the other person thinks. It was #9 among paid Business apps on the US App Store on 7 November.

item.title: ShiftBoard puts firefighter and EMT shift rotations on one calendar
item.description: ShiftBoard shows every shift rotation you work or track on one calendar, with ready-made rotations like 24/48 and 48/96, for firefighters, paramedics, EMTs and 911 dispatchers. It was #30 among paid Productivity apps on the US App Store on 7 November.

item.title: GoaTime combines your tasks, daily plan and time tracking
item.description: GoaTime brings personal tasks, projects, daily planning and time tracking together, so you see your next step and where your time goes. It was #38 among paid Productivity apps on the US App Store on 7 November.

item.title: Leash Lookout maps your dog-walking route house by house
item.description: Leash Lookout turns your daily dog walk into a map you keep, house by house, with the people you pass and the help you might need one tap away. It was #39 among paid Lifestyle apps on the US App Store on 7 November.

item.title: IronFox is a simple workout log that shows your progress
item.description: IronFox lets you log workouts and see how your fitness is progressing over time. It was #44 among paid Health & Fitness apps on the US App Store on 7 November.

item.title: ¡Hola Ola! teaches the Spanish you need on a beach trip
item.description: ¡Hola Ola! teaches travel Spanish for coastal trips: hailing a taxi, checking into a hostel, ordering dinner, making friends and renting a surfboard. It was #60 among paid Travel apps on the US App Store on 7 November.

item.title: Hills Ahead shows your road trip from the side, hills and all
item.description: Hills Ahead draws your car trip as a side view: start on the left, destination on the right, the road rising and falling with the real terrain, and a little car moving along as you drive. It was #59 among paid Travel apps on the US App Store on 7 November.

item.title: Mountain Visibility Forecast tells you if the mountain will be out
item.description: Mountain Visibility Forecast predicts whether a mountain will be visible from where you are, beyond what the window shows. It was #24 among paid Weather apps on the US App Store on 7 November.

item.title: Inyo Notes saves everything you write to its day
item.description: Inyo is a notes app organized by day: it opens ready to write, and each entry with text, photos, links and tags is saved to its day. It was #61 among paid Productivity apps on the US App Store on 7 November.

item.title: warmread is a teleprompter that follows your voice
item.description: warmread scrolls your script as you talk, waits when you pause and keeps your place when you ad-lib; the next lines glow so your eyes stay ahead. It was #60 among paid Productivity apps on the US App Store on 7 November.

item.title: Biblio Times lays out your news feeds as a morning newspaper
item.description: Biblio Times collects the public feeds of the publications you choose each morning and lays them out as a newspaper with a front page, sections and columns. It was #45 among free News apps on the US App Store on 7 November.

item.title: Recipe Lab Studio develops camera RAW photos on your iPhone, one payment
item.description: Recipe Lab Studio takes the RAW files from your camera and develops them on your phone, with no computer, account or subscription. It was #60 among paid Photo & Video apps on the US App Store on 7 November.

item.title: Nāda Brahma: sound meditation with real gongs, bowls and chimes
item.description: Nāda Brahma is a sound-meditation app built on recordings of real instruments, like gongs, singing bowls, crystal, chimes and handpan, with moving visuals. It was #40 among paid Lifestyle apps on the US App Store on 7 November.

item.title: Channel Launcher puts UK live TV channels in one guide
item.description: Channel Launcher is a live TV guide for iPhone, iPad and Apple TV that brings UK channels like BBC together and opens the right app to watch. It was #31 among all paid apps on the UK App Store on 7 November.

item.title: Starlink price increase: surge pricing raises some US plans 10-20%
item.description: SpaceX emailed Starlink customers across the US that Residential prices are going up 10% to 20% in busy areas, saying it needs to manage supply and demand. The Residential Max plan goes from $130 to $156 a month at 20%.

item.title: iOS 27 HDMI problem: video stops when you lock your iPhone
item.description: On iOS 27, many iPhone owners report that video to an external display over HDMI stops once the phone is locked. GSMArena reproduced it with YouTube and Netflix; VLC still works.

item.title: YouTube TV support scam: fake phone number on Google cost a viewer thousands
item.description: A YouTube TV viewer in North Carolina lost several thousand dollars after calling a fake support number found on Google, the McDowell County Sheriff's Office says. The caller was told to buy Lowe's gift cards.

item.title: BabyBackup turns two phones or iPads into a baby monitor
item.description: BabyBackup makes a baby monitor from two devices you already own: one stays with your baby, you keep the other and listen. It was #10 among paid Lifestyle apps on the US App Store on 6 November.
